data: Does the recursive implementation always converge faster to 93% accuracy compared to the iterative implementation?

The question asks whether the recursive implementation always converges faster to 93% accuracy compared to the iterative implementation. From the caption, we know that the time to reach 93% accuracy for each setup is also plotted, and it is stated that the recursive implementation converges faster for all models. This means that the red line (recursive) consistently reaches the dotted line (93% accuracy) before the blue line (iterative). 

Looking at the graphs, we can see that this is indeed the case for all three models (TreeRNN, RNTN, and TreeLSTM). In each subfigure, the red line (recursive) crosses the dotted line (93% accuracy) before the blue line (iterative). Therefore, the answer to the question is yes, the recursive implementation always converges faster to 93% accuracy compared to the iterative implementation.
